Key fact: Telogen effluvium shedding typically begins 2 to 3 months after the triggering event, not immediately. What Causes Telogen Effluvium? Telogen effluvium happens when a stressor pushes many hair follicles into a resting phase at once. Normally, follicles cycle through growth and rest at different times. social_media_tags.twitter:title: The DHT Connection in Perimenopausal Hair Thinning
social_media_tags.twitter:description: DHT is the hormone most linked to hair loss in women. It stands for dihydrotestosterone. Estrogen normally keeps DHT's effects on hair follicles in check. That balance shifts during perimenopause. Key fact: A 2023 randomized, placebo-controlled trial found saw palmetto, which targets the DHT-producing enzyme, reduced hair fall over 16 weeks. What Hormone Causes Hair Loss in Women? DHT (dihydrotestosterone) is the hormone most closely linked to hair loss in women. DHT is made from testosterone by an enzyme called 5-alpha-reductase. Every woman has some testosterone and some DHT. Hair loss is not usually about having too much DHT. It is usually about how sensitive your hair follicles are to it. social_media_tags.og:title: Is This Normal Shedding or Something Else?
social_media_tags.og:description: Learn how much daily hair shedding is normal, why shower shedding looks worse than it is, and how to run a simple at-home self-check.
social_media_tags.twitter:title: Is This Normal Shedding or Something Else?
social_media_tags.twitter:description: Losing about 100 hairs a day is normal. Most people do not notice this because it is spread throughout the day. Shedding becomes noticeable when it goes well above that number. A simple self-check can help you tell the difference. Key fact: The average scalp has about 100,000 hair follicles, and losing up to 100 hairs a day is considered normal turnover. How Much Hair Loss Is Normal in a Day? About 100 hairs a day is the commonly cited normal range. Some days you may lose fewer, and some days more. Hair grows in cycles, so shedding happens on a rolling basis. Roughly 90 percent of your hair is in an active growth phase at any time. The remaining hair is resting or preparing to shed. This turnover is a normal, healthy process, not a sign of a problem.
